newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 28.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Pioneer
BHARATIYA JANATA PARTY RULES OUT ALLIANCE

Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) president L.K.Advani said he did not see the party reaching an understanding with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) in Uttar Pradesh, despite informal exchanges between the two. Advani said the BJP should be called to form a government as the single largest party in the local assembly, should the Samajwadi Party and the BSP fail to arrive at an understanding.
The Hindustan Times
DEVE GOWDA ANNOUNCES 61 BLN RUPEE PACKAGE FOR NORTH-EAST

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda announced a 61 billion rupee package for Northeast India. He said the only way out of unemployment and militancy was economic development of the region. Deve Gowda said all ministries would earmark at least 10 percent of their Plan funds for the region. He said a commission would be appointed within 60 days to examine gaps in sectors like power, communications, railways, roads, education and agriculture.
The Economic Times
FRESH GUIDELINES TO AID PORT PRIVATISATION

The surface transport ministry recently opened the country's major ports for private investment. New guidelines will set up a regulatory body for fixing and revising port tariffs once every three years. Private investment has been allowed in the construction and operation of container terminals, bulk, break bulk, multipurpose and specialised cargo berths, warehousing, container freight stations, storage facilities, dry docking, ship-repairing and dredging. Private parties would also be invited set up captive power plants at the ports, the surplus from which could be sold outside the port arena.
STALLED POWER PROJECTS TO BE REVIEWED

The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) would review power sector projects involving foreign equity which have failed to emerge up despite getting approvals several years ago. This would kick-off the FIPB's objective to survey a host of sectors where projects have not materialised yet. Official sources said the FIPB would be studying only large projects approved till 1995. The board would then take corrective action and speed up necessary clearances. Industry ministry sources, in fact, pointed to the need for a single-window clearance system, where FIPB could clear a host of applications required for a single project.
INDIAN OIL CORP TO DIVERSIFY INTO PORT INFRASTRUCTURE

The Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) is planning a foray into port infrastructure, including jetties and tankages at several locations. Though plans are yet to be approved, initial estimates point to investments of around five billion rupees in the next two years. The IOC would be routing this effort through its existing joint venture partner Oil Tanking of Germany. In other initiatives, the IOC will be the canalising agency for import of naphtha for power generation. These efforts are in addition to plans for diversifying into petrochemicals, setting up power plants in the vicinity of IOC refineries, as well as importing and supplying LNG.
CENTRAL BANK LIMITS BANKS' EXPOSURE

The central bank (RBI) limited commercial banks' total exposure to a company to 25 percent of the net owned funds of the bank and 30 percent of the company's paid-up capital. This includes investments in shares and debentures in primary or secondary markets as well as advances. A central bank circular said investment in shares and debentures must be included within the prudential exposure limits and the statutory stipulations for investment in companies. This puts into effect the RBI's policy statement allowing banks to invest in the secondary market within the existing limit of five percent of the previous fiscal year's incremental deposits.
Financial Express
SELECTION OF MERCHANT BANKERS QUESTIONED

Communications Minister Beni Prasad Verma questioned the selection of Solomon Brothers, Klienwort Benson and Jardine Fleming as merchant bankers for Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd's (VSNL) global depository receipt (GDR)-cum-divestment issue. The Core Group of Secretaries, formed to oversee the government's divestments in VSNL and Indian Oil Corp, had recommended the three merchant bankers be given the mandate to manage the VSNL issue. Ministry sources said Verma might not have been happy about the reported lack of transparency in the selection of the merchant bankers' consortium.
